title: Lazygit Alternative for Files and Git | Forge TUI
description: Looking for a Lazygit alternative with a file tree, code search and embedded terminal? Compare workflows and choose a Git TUI for your project.
alt: Side-by-side diff in Forge Git panel
lead: Forge TUI is a Lazygit alternative for developers who need file navigation and code review alongside Git operations. Lazygit is a dedicated terminal Git UI; Forge brings a repository file tree, previews, search and shell tabs into the same workspace.
sections: Choose based on your workflow

Choose Lazygit when the main job is Git and you already have a preferred editor or file manager. Consider Forge when a review sends you from a diff to another source file, then to a shell for a test. Forge keeps those activities in one interface rather than claiming to replace every Lazygit feature.
Review a change with source context

Open a repository with forge. Select a changed file in Git, inspect the full-file diff, and switch to Files to read neighboring implementation or search for callers. Return to Git to stage or unstage the intended changes. This is useful for a patch spanning several modules.
Run tests alongside the review

Use an embedded terminal tab for project commands while keeping the file tree and Git review nearby. Run cargo test in a Rust project, or the existing test command in another project. After reviewing the result, inspect staged changes before committing.
Mouse and platform support

Forge offers clicks, context menus, resizable panels, scrollbars and keyboard shortcuts. Native Windows x64, Linux and macOS release packages are available. Check the current guide for effective controls; terminal behavior can vary.
When to keep Lazygit

Forge is not a drop-in clone of Lazygit. Advanced Git workflows may be better handled by a dedicated Git client or the Git CLI. Compare both on a real repository before switching; no comparative performance claim is made here.

title: Yazi Alternative for Git-Focused Workflows | Forge TUI
description: Compare Yazi and Forge TUI for file browsing, previews, mouse support and Git review. Choose a terminal file manager for your workflow.
alt: Forge file tree with syntax-highlighted code preview
lead: If you are looking for a Yazi alternative because you spend most of your time reviewing code changes, Forge TUI offers a repository-focused workspace with file navigation, Git diffs, search and embedded terminals. Yazi remains a capable general-purpose terminal file manager.
sections: Choose Yazi for general file management

Yazi supports previews, bulk file operations, mouse interaction, Git integration and an extensible plugin ecosystem. Choose it when broad file-management capabilities and customization are the priority. Consult its upstream documentation for individual plugins and platform requirements.
Choose Forge for repository review

Forge connects source navigation and Git review. Inspect syntax-highlighted files, search across the project, open a changed file as a visual diff, stage changes and browse commit history. Run repository commands in the embedded shell.
Try a repository-first workflow

Open a repository with uncommitted changes. In Forge, find a source file, inspect its preview, then switch to Git and review the corresponding diff. Search for related code and run the relevant test command in Terminal. Stage only changes you intend. This helps evaluate whether the integrated workflow reduces tool switching.
Mouse and platform support

Both tools offer mouse interaction. Forge provides clickable panels, context menus, draggable dividers and scrollbars. Native Windows x64 builds are available alongside Linux and macOS releases. Evaluate input and clipboard behavior in your own terminal.
What Forge does not replace

Forge does not claim Yazi plugin compatibility, equivalent support for every preview format, or superiority in general file operations. If you rely on Yazi-specific plugins or advanced file management, keep Yazi and use Forge for repository review when helpful.

title: A Terminal Workspace for Codex CLI | Forge TUI
description: Run Codex CLI in a terminal while browsing files, searching code and reviewing Git diffs in Forge TUI.
alt: Forge embedded terminal alongside project files
lead: A coding agent can modify many files during a session. Forge provides a separate file and Git view alongside an embedded terminal for manual inspection.
sections: Set up
Install Forge and Codex CLI separately. Start Forge in the target repository, open Terminal (F8 by default), and run codex if it is installed on PATH.
Review agent changes
Switch to Git (F2) to inspect modified paths and full-file diffs. Use Files or search to read surrounding code; Ctrl+R refreshes if needed. Stage only intended changes.
Validate independently
Use another shell tab for tests and lint commands. Inspect the output yourself before committing. Keep credentials and permissions under your control.
Compatibility boundary
Forge embeds a terminal, not a Codex API integration. Interactive behavior depends on the host terminal and Forge version. It does not manage Codex authentication or approvals.

title: A Terminal Workspace for Claude Code | Forge TUI
description: Use Claude Code in a Forge TUI shell alongside a project tree, code search and Git diffs for manual review.
alt: Forge terminal tab alongside a project workspace
lead: Claude Code runs in a terminal; Forge provides surrounding project navigation and Git review, keeping the agent session and your own inspection distinct.
sections: Launch in a project
Install Claude Code separately and ensure claude is on PATH. Run forge in the repository, open Terminal with F8 and launch claude. Configure authentication and permissions in Claude Code.
Inspect changes
Open Git to see changed paths and inspect full-file diffs. Use code search to find affected references. Refresh with Ctrl+R if needed; review before staging.
Run independent checks
Use another shell tab for the project test suite. Keep the agent session available while comparing results and manually reviewing uncertain changes.
No special integration required
Forge does not supply Claude Code, intercept approvals, or guarantee compatibility with every terminal feature. It is a local file, Git and terminal workspace.

title: Terminal Git Client for Windows, Linux and macOS | Forge TUI
description: Use Forge as a terminal Git client with visual diffs, staging, commit history and file navigation. Native Windows x64, Linux and macOS builds.
lead: Forge is an open-source terminal Git client that combines visual diffs and staging with the project file tree, search and embedded shells. Native Windows x64 packages are available, so Windows users do not need WSL to run Forge.
sections: Install on Windows Terminal or PowerShell

Install Git for Windows, then use the Windows PowerShell installer on the Forge homepage or download the Windows x64 ZIP from GitHub Releases. The installer verifies the release checksum and adds Forge to your user PATH. Open a new terminal, change into a repository and run forge. WSL users can install the Linux build separately.
Review before staging
Open Git with F2, select a changed file and inspect its diff with surrounding code. Navigate to Files to examine other source files and use search to locate references.
Stage and commit
Use the Git panel's contextual actions to stage or unstage selected changes. Review staged content, open the commit dialog, enter a message and commit only what you intend.
History and branch workflows
Browse commit history, blame, branches and stashes. Use the built-in shell for advanced Git commands or automation. Check F4 for effective shortcuts.
Who it is for
Useful for developers working over SSH, in WSL or locally who want visual Git review and file access in one TUI. Forge does not replace every Git command.
Review AI-generated changes before committing

If you run a coding assistant in a shell, inspect its changes in the Git panel before staging. Use the file preview and content search to read surrounding code, then run the project test command in Terminal. Forge provides the review workspace; the coding assistant itself is installed and run separately.

title: Terminal File Manager with Mouse Support and Git | Forge TUI
description: A terminal file manager with mouse support, Git integration, code previews and content search. Browse repositories on Windows, Linux and macOS.
alt: Forge directory tree and code preview
lead: Forge TUI is a terminal file manager with mouse support and Git integration for developers working inside source repositories. Its project tree, code preview, search and Git panel share a single workspace.
sections: Browse and preview
Run forge in a project directory. Expand folders in the Files panel, open source files in the preview and inspect Markdown or syntax-highlighted code without launching a separate editor.
Find files and content
Use Ctrl+P for file-name search or the Search panel for content matches. Open a match at its line to inspect the relevant code.
Mouse and keyboard
Click and double-click items, open context menus, drag panel dividers and scrollbars, and scroll content. Terminal mouse support and key bindings can vary; use F4 to view effective shortcuts.
Connect files with Git
Switch to Git to inspect changes to the same repository. Forge is designed for developer workflows rather than replacing every general-purpose file manager.
Use Forge on native Windows

The Windows x64 release runs in a modern Windows terminal without WSL. Use the same project-oriented file browsing and Git review workflow. Git must be installed separately for Git operations; the host terminal controls supported mouse reporting and clipboard features.

title: Integrated Terminal for a Git and File Workspace | Forge TUI
description: Run interactive CLI tools and shells in Forge TUI while keeping your project tree, code search and Git review nearby.
alt: Forge terminal panel with shell tabs
lead: Forge embeds interactive terminal sessions inside the same TUI as file navigation and Git review. It is useful for running project commands while inspecting code.
sections: Open a shell
Launch forge in your working directory and open Terminal (F8 by default). Run the commands you normally use for development, such as git status, cargo test or npm test.
Separate tasks with tabs
Keep a shell for builds and another for interactive CLI work. Return to Files or Git when you need to inspect changes. Check the guide for the current tab and focus controls.
Pointer and keyboard behavior
Use context-aware shortcuts and mouse interaction. Programs inside a terminal can handle their own input; clipboard, selection and mouse behavior depend on the host and running program.
What it is not
Forge is not an agent service or an OS terminal emulator replacement. Install your shell and CLI tools separately; Forge provides a project-centered workspace around them.
